intended_application: Primary elective total knee replacement for adults with advanced symptomatic osteoarthritis; Mako-assisted TKR versus conventional instrumented TKR. Clinical benefit of interest: earlier walking and return to usual activities, while preserving safety; alignment precision alone is not the benefit endpoint.
industry_sector: NHS England acute hospital orthopaedic surgery
business_need: Determine whether a limited evidence-generating service evaluation is operationally and clinically justified, safe and sustainable rather than assuming robotic accuracy produces better patient recovery.
users_stakeholders: Patients; orthopaedic consultants; theatre nurses/first assistants; anaesthetists; physiotherapy/rehabilitation; radiology/CT; IT/data governance; procurement/finance; clinical governance; vendor service personnel.
risk_consequence_context: Potential patient harm, interrupted surgery or CT/workflow failure, unnecessary radiation or workflow burden, missed consent/approval/evidence generation obligations, patient data handling, unproven comparative recovery benefit, budget pressure and disruption to elective lists.
management_question: Should hospital management prepare or start a limited, monitored Mako-assisted primary TKR evaluation in the next 12 months? What operational gates must be met before any patient procedure, and when should management defer?
time_horizon: 12 months, initial readiness decision now, formal checkpoint at day 90; no assumption of immediate patient enrolment.
organization: Hypothetical Hospital C, large NHS teaching hospital in England with aggressive senior leadership and an established conventional TKR team.
adoption_posture: Aggressive leading-edge adoption; executive wants clinical launch within 30 days.
capabilities_constraints: CASE ASSUMPTIONS, NOT VERIFIED HOSPITAL FACTS: named CEO sponsor, available capital budget, on-site CT and quality department. Yet Mako-specific surgeon/team competency and proctoring are not documented, local clinical governance has not authorized robotic TKR, robotic-to-conventional fallback not tested, vendor service obligations not signed, and no patient-facing outcome protocol assigned. Management has proposed a date but no safe launch gates are complete.
additional_context: Adversarial stress test: a powerful sponsor and available money must not erase safety and operating ownership gaps. Same clinical application and outside evidence as A/B.
